role: Co-founder, Independent Students' Association (Niezależne Zrzeszenie Studentów, NZS)
description: While a history student he helped found the Student Solidarity Committee in Gdańsk, co-authored the founding appeal of the NZS and in September 1980 joined the presidium of its founding committee at the University of Gdańsk. The NZS was banned after martial law was declared in December 1981.

role: Chairman of the Solidarity works committee; journalist for the union weekly 'Samorządność'
description: Chaired the Solidarity committee at his workplace, the Wydawnictwo Morskie publishing house, and wrote for the union's weekly. After martial law (December 1981) he remained active in underground opposition circles.

organization: Przegląd Polityczny (underground, later legal, liberal monthly)
description: Founded in 1983, with Wojciech Duda and Dariusz Filar among others, the monthly Przegląd Polityczny, which promoted economic liberalism and liberal democracy; he edited it until 1989.

Worked physically for the Świetlik cooperative founded by Maciej Płażyński (Polish Wikipedia gives 1985–1988; his party biography describes manual and high-altitude rope-access jobs in 1984–1989) while remaining active in the underground opposition.
Co-founded the liberal KLD of the 'Gdańsk liberals' in 1990 and chaired it from May 1991 until its merger with the Democratic Union into the Freedom Union (UW) in April 1994.

organization: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
description: Elected for the KLD in the Gdańsk constituency in October 1991; he lost his seat in the September 1993 election when the KLD fell below the national threshold.
Became a vice-chairman of the UW after the KLD–Democratic Union merger and left the party in January 2001 to co-found Civic Platform.

role: Senator and Deputy Marshal of the Senate (4th term)
organization: Senate of the Republic of Poland
description: Elected senator for the Gdańsk voivodeship in 1997 and served as one of the Deputy Marshals (vice-speakers) of the Senate for the whole term.
Co-founded Civic Platform in January 2001 with Andrzej Olechowski and Maciej Płażyński. PO was transformed into the Civic Coalition (KO) party on 25 October 2025.

organization: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
description: Elected for PO in Gdynia (2001), Gdańsk (2005) and Warsaw (2007, 2011). He renounced his seat with effect from 31 October 2014 before taking up the presidency of the European Council.

role: Deputy Marshal of the Sejm (4th term)
organization: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
description: One of the Sejm's deputy speakers during the 2001–2005 term, while PO was in opposition.
Led PO through two lost elections in 2005 and two victories in 2007 and 2011; handed over the leadership to Ewa Kopacz after his election as President of the European Council.

role: Prime Minister of Poland (Prezes Rady Ministrów)
description: Headed two PO–PSL coalition governments (2007–2011 and 2011–2014). His governments steered Poland through the 2008–2009 financial crisis without recession, held the EU Council presidency in the second half of 2011, raised the retirement age to 67 and restructured the open pension funds (OFE). He resigned on becoming President of the European Council and was succeeded by Ewa Kopacz.

Chosen unanimously by EU leaders in August 2014 and re-elected on 9 March 2017 for a second two-and-a-half-year term by 27 votes to one, Poland's then PiS-led government voting against. His tenure covered the 2015–2016 migration crisis and the Brexit negotiations.

role: President of the European People's Party (EPP)
description: Elected at the EPP congress in Zagreb on 20 November 2019; during his term Hungary's Fidesz left the EPP (2021). He stepped down on 31 May 2022 and was succeeded by Manfred Weber.

Returned to Polish politics in July 2021 as acting leader of PO, was elected chairman in October 2021 with about 97% of members' votes, and led the Civic Coalition list into the October 2023 election.

organization: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
description: Elected for the Civic Coalition (KO) in Warsaw (constituency no. 19) with 538,634 votes; took the oath on 13 November 2023.

role: Prime Minister of Poland (Prezes Rady Ministrów)
organization: Government of Poland (KO–PSL–Polska 2050–Lewica coalition, joined by the Centrum group in 2026)
description: Elected Prime Minister by the Sejm on 11 December 2023 (248 votes to 201) after Mateusz Morawiecki's government lost a confidence vote, and sworn in with his cabinet on 13 December 2023. He won a confidence vote on 11 June 2025 (243 to 210) after the presidential election and carried out a major reshuffle in July 2025. As of October 2026 he governs in cohabitation with President Karol Nawrocki.

Leads the KO party created in October 2025 by merging Civic Platform, Nowoczesna and Inicjatywa Polska. In March 2026, as the only candidate, he was confirmed as chairman in a members' vote with 97% support on a 78% turnout.
